message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$8,912 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and funded entirely from existing cash with no money moved out). Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year FY2024 net sales of $391.0B with net income of $93.7B, or $6.08 diluted EPS — figures I confirmed against the SEC 10-K filed Nov 1, 2024 (the EPS includes a one-time $10.2B tax charge, so underlying earnings power is stronger than the headline). News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, which suggests expectations are modest rather than euphoric. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), my limit of $222.80 was essentially at market, satisfying the "close to current market price" requirement. I sized the position modestly (~18% of available cash) given the mixed near-term demand signals, keeping room to add on weakness.
